page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highcpu-48 is an arm64-based virtual machine offering 48 dedicated virtual CPUs and 96.0 GB of system memory. Its hardware topology establishes a ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per core, emphasizing processing throughput over large memory footprints.

The instance does not include integrated local SSD storage, requiring persistent disk attachments over the network for file system operations. In addition, the instance contains no GPU hardware acceleration and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, pointing to a backend deployment model within managed networks.

Resource allocation on the n4a-highcpu-48 yields favorable cost efficiency for compute-intensive tasks, as infrastructure spend is concentrated on dedicated cores rather than excess memory capacity. The tradeoff is reduced suitability for memory-resident datasets and dependence on network storage latency for persistent input/output.

Suitable workloads for this configuration include parallelized batch compute, continuous integration compilation tasks targeting Arm environments, media transcoding, stateless API services, and distributed compute worker pools.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highcpu-48 is a compute-focused virtual machine powered by 64-bit Arm architecture. The configuration supplies 48 dedicated virtual CPUs and 96.0 GB of memory, providing a core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It features no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for data persistence, and operates without discrete GPU accelerators. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing execution without resource sharing. By minimizing memory overhead per core, the instance delivers high compute density for organizations seeking cost-efficient throughput on parallelized applications. The profile aligns with CPU-bound processing, multi-threaded continuous integration and build workloads, distributed computation nodes, and containerized microservices optimized for the Arm instruction set.
